sources.entry: Komga - Media server for comics/mangas/BDs with API and OPDS support, a modern web interface for exploring your libraries, as well as a web reader. (Source Code) MIT Java/Docker
Komga | Media server for comics, manga and ebooks

summary.one_liner: Komga is a self-hosted media server for comics, manga, BDs, magazines and eBooks, with a web UI, web reader, REST API and OPDS feeds.
summary.what_it_does: Komga organizes comic, manga, BD, magazine and eBook files into libraries, series and books, and lets you browse them through a responsive web interface that works on desktop, tablet and phone. It includes a web reader with multiple reading modes and supports collections and read lists, including importing ComicRack cbl read lists. It can edit series and book metadata and import embedded metadata automatically. Multi-user access supports per-library access control, age restrictions and label restrictions. It also offers OPDS v1 and v2 support, a REST API, Kobo Sync and KOReader Sync, plus file downloads for books, whole series or read lists, and duplicate file and duplicate page detection.
use_cases: self-host a comic and manga library
sync books to a Kobo eReader
serve comics to OPDS reader apps
manage multi-user access to a digital library
find and remove duplicate comic files or pages
how_to_run: Refer to the website for installation instructions (the README does not include commands).
notable: Kobo Sync and KOReader Sync support for e-reader devices
OPDS v1 and v2 catalog support
Duplicate file and duplicate page detection and removal
Per-library, age and label-based access restrictions for multiple users
caveats: The README defers installation and documentation details to an external website
Specific system requirements and platform support are not stated in the README
